rejected.title: Ways to improve liveability
card: Liveability is how well a place meets the needs of the people who live there. A place can be made more liveable by changing things in it.
Transport
Better buses, trains, footpaths and bike paths help people get to school, work and shops more easily.
Parks and trees
Parks, green space and street trees give people places to play and relax. Trees also give shade and help keep an area cooler.
Other ways
Safer streets (such as better lighting and safe crossings), affordable housing and community facilities (such as libraries and sports centres) also make a place more liveable.
rejected.remember: Liveability improves when a place gets better transport, green space, safety, housing and facilities.

a.q: People in a new housing estate say summer days are very hot and there is nowhere shady to sit outside. Which change would best help them?
opts: Planting shady trees and opening green space
Adding an extra bus route to the city
Building more affordable homes nearby
Putting brighter lights along the footpaths
a.why: Trees give shade and help keep an area cooler, and green space gives people somewhere to relax outside. Brighter lights make streets safer at night, but they do nothing about heat or shade.
a.clue: Focus on the problem the residents describe: heat and no shade.

b.q: Many people in the town of Tallowbrook say they feel unsafe walking home after dark. Which change would best improve liveability for them?
opts: Better street lighting and safe crossings
A new weekend bus timetable for the town
More affordable rental homes in the town
A larger library with more computers
b.why: Better lighting and safe crossings make streets safer, which deals with the problem people describe. Affordable homes, a library and buses can improve liveability in other ways, but they do not fix feeling unsafe at night.
b.clue: Match the change to the problem the residents describe.

a.q: A council plants street trees and builds a new park in a suburb. Which way of improving liveability is this?
opts: Adding parks and trees
Improving public transport
Making housing more affordable
Building a community facility
a.why: Street trees and a park are green space, which gives people shade and places to relax. A park is not a community facility such as a library or sports centre, so that option is not the best fit.
a.clue: Think about what trees and parks add to an area.
